explanation: Computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to balance cost and performance.  Faster, smaller, and more expensive memory (like cache) sits closer to the CPU, while slower, larger, and cheaper memory (like main memory and disk) resides further away. Caching strategies leverage this hierarchy to minimize access time to frequently used data. Data is copied from lower levels to higher levels as needed, improving overall system performance.
syntax: Cache organization is typically described by parameters like size, associativity (set-associative, direct-mapped, fully-associative), and replacement policy (LRU, FIFO, random).  Performance is evaluated using metrics like hit rate, miss rate, and average memory access time (AMAT).
